$comment: The issue board's data model (plan/RULES.md §2-§3). fixOf: a fix to an earlier plan's work names the landed issue it fixes, { issue, title?, board } (embed.js sets board from the folders on disk; plan/RULES.md §1), else null. new.js copies this file, fills the header fields, and empties rows, milestones, trail, followUps and documents; every value still written <like this> is a placeholder that check.js refuses. The three rows show the shapes: an issue board's row (all four option verdicts), a Left-for-later row, and a tracking board's unit row (kind tracking only). The Verdict and As built cells are lists of statements (plan/RULES.md §2, "Statements"): verdict.statements, one decision each, ending with ref, the relative link to the plan section it rests on ("plan.md#<GitHub heading anchor>", or the plan-<unit>.md it came from; architecture.md for a unit row), bullets or, with verdict.list "numbered", numbered when the order matters; asBuilt.statements, one per verdict statement in the same order, each with its adaptation as state (as-planned | amended | deviated), from which the row's outcome is derived. Each statement's excerpt {ref, heading, paragraph, hash} is copied by embed.js from the section its ref names and never written by hand; check.js warns once that section has changed since. A verdict written before the statements keeps one paragraph in verdict.summary. Links to other issues' boards are never written by hand: embed.js sets parent.board (on a sub-issue's board, {"issue": n, "board": "../dashboard.html" or null}), each unit's unit.board, and issueBoards ({"<issue>": "<path to its dashboard.html>"} for every other issue the board names whose board exists in the tree), from the folders on disk (plan/RULES.md §1). On a tracking board, embed.js also writes unit.live on each unit in wip.current: a mirror of that sub-issue board's run (its wip step, since, updated, detail, steps, waitingOn, resume, qa, qaMax, and its status and branch), refreshed at every embed of either board and never written by hand (plan/RULES.md §3). level, unit.level and wip.proposedLevel keep the work level as data only, for the scripts: no board shows them, and no text on a board names a work level (GUIDANCE.md §4; check.js fails it). Until an excerpt is copied, embed.js writes the statement's refNumber {ref, label, from}: the section number its anchor names, read from the referenced file's headings (from headings: GitHub's anchor drops the dots, so 42-… is §4.2 or §42 and the headings decide), else the anchor's leading number, from anchor, which the board marks "§42?"; never written by hand. sized is the run's start (an ISO date-time): new.js stamps it at the foundation, apply-event.js at sized on a board laid before its run (null until then), and the Timeline tile of a landed board reads it with the verdict milestone, the qa passes' at (else date) and asBuilt.date for its phases (plan/RULES.md §2, "The KPI tiles"). Delete every $comment.
title: <short name of the change>
issueTitle: <the issue's title, verbatim: never reworded or elided; one that names a work level is a defect in the issue, flagged>
function: <one paragraph: what the issue asked, and what this run does about it>
sized: <ISO date-time the run was sized: new.js stamps it at the foundation, apply-event.js at sized on a board laid before its run>

wip.$comment: step: sizing | interview | research | architecture | plan | branch | implementation | qa | remediation | document | landing | merge | landed | halted | escalated | cancelled (state-boards: a board that reached its landing before dashboards-skill/35). document: the Document step's tasks, { tasks: [{ id, name, state }] }, ids documentation-review | reconcile-documentation | dokka-check | reconcile-plan | readme-changelog | state-boards, state done | current | todo, several current at once where they run in parallel; the document event writes it. open[]: { text, raised, ref, copy?, resolved? }: a ref naming a build output outside the tree is plain text, copy the path of the report's copy under docs/plans/.live/open/ the live view links; every open point is resolved at the landing. qa[]: its report, the test report's path (build/reports/tests/index.html, plain text), reportCopy its live copy. current: <row-id>.<column> addresses or a column name (gap, considered, verdict, built), the work in progress, exactly the cells being worked on however many (no count limit); it follows step by the step-to-column map (plan/RULES.md §3): interview the cell the question concerns or nothing, research the <row-id>.considered cells of the rows the questions being researched or verified name , between the last return and the verification the returned questions' rows (the whole considered column only while the rows are unknown: no question recorded, none researching, verifying or returned, or a glowing question naming no row; an issue board at research with no rows once its research has started is a defect, NO ROWS AT RESEARCH, as its rows are named from the gaps before the research starts; during research planning, with no question recorded yet, considered on a board with rows and nothing on a board with none), architecture considered, plan (writing or verifying a plan) considered and verdict, implementation and remediation the touched rows <row-id>.built (a tracking board: its units in progress), and the whole As built column, built, for an implementation stage that touches no rows (such as the as-built record) or while no stage is current, qa built, a tracking board's sub-issues and boards the label cell of each unit row not yet done in the step (<unit-id>.units: a unit with no issue yet, then one with no board yet; each stops glowing as it is done), sizing, branch, landing, landed and cancelled nothing; halted and escalated keep the glow of the step in resume, held still. A column address (gap, considered, verdict, built) is drawn as one glow on the column itself, its band and head (on the As built tab, round the cards; on a phone, where no columns are drawn, on each of its cells), never each row's cell lit; a <row-id>.<column> address lights its cell. next: on a tracking board only, the id of the next unit in landing order (the first unit row that is pending, not in current and not left for later: a unit whose verdict is kind leave is skipped), or null when none is left; it is kept so at every landing and every unit start, so the board always names what is coming. On a tracking board, step is the tracking issue's own phase: implementation while its units run (each unit's own step is in its row's unit.live), never a unit's step. While halted: resume (the step to return to) and waitingOn. The step panel's facts (plan/RULES.md §3, "The step panel"), each optional: event, the last event {name, at, note}; interview, the interview's questions {text, options: the options it offers (from the halted event's facts.questions), answer: null while it waits, asked, answered}; research {phase: planning | research | verification | complete, drafted: the questions drafted so far, since: {<phase>: when it began}}; questions, the research questions {question: <slug>, rows: [<row-id>], findings: null until it returns, then the findings path, state: planning | researching | returned | verifying | complete, started, returned}, written by research-started, research-returned, verification-started and researched, kept complete until plan-accepted (on a tracking board, architecture-signed-off), which clears them with research; plan {state: writing | re-pass, from: parent | qa | existing (a re-pass's source: the parent's plan, a qa pass, or an existing plan verified against the base), pass: the qa pass a re-pass answers, against: the ref an existing plan is verified against (e.g. main), since}; stages, the implementation stages of plan.md {id, name, state: done | current | todo, rows}; open, the run's open points {text, raised: the event or stage that raised it, ref: a link (optional), resolved: how it was settled, left out while open}, listed in the step panel until resolved, then kept in the trail; remediation {pass: the qa pass it answers, route: on-the-spot | remediation | re-plan-then-remediation (rookie-dev and planner-then-rookie-dev, the older ids, read alike), steps: [{name, state}] (what is the older name of name)}. qa[].verdict: approved | changes-requested | running; qa[].findings counts by kind, qa[].severity by severity (minor: easily made, no fallout; other), qa[].route the route step 5 takes from them; qaMax the most passes (3). blockers from the tracker's blocked-by links; repo only when another repository's. history (plan/RULES.md §3, "Finished steps"): each finished step's visits, oldest first, frozen by apply-event.js as each ended, never written by hand: { since: when the visit began (when the visit before it ended), ended, endedBy: the event that ended it, to: the step the run moved to, held: true when it ended while the run waited on the user, event: its last event, detail: its last detail line, open: the open points still open, and the step's own facts as they stood (lib.js HISTORY_FIELDS): interview; research and questions; plan; branch; stages; qa, the passes of the visit (every qa verdict is a visit of qa); remediation with qa, the pass it answers (every remediation loop is a visit of its own); units {done, total} at sub-issues and boards }. A finished step with no snapshot (it ended before the snapshots) is reconstructed on the board from the trail, the milestones, the stages and the qa passes.

options.name: <an option left open at plan time>
options.why: <why it was left open; column 4 settles it with a change carrying settles>

statements.text: <one decision, in a sentence: what the work does to this part>
statements.ref: <plan.md#heading-anchor: the plan section it rests on>

steps.what: <one sentence naming the file and anchor>
steps.check: <the command or observation that proves it>

tests: <Level n — the class and the claim>

asBuilt.$comment: state: pending | in-progress | partially-built | as-planned | amended | deviated | dropped | deferred | complete | landed. Before the outcome (plan/RULES.md §2): while the run is live, wip.stages decide it until the row's last stage is done (a current stage: in-progress; a done stage and a later one to come: partially-built, its summary saying what is built and what is left; only stages to come: pending), and the board derives it; a unit in wip.current reads in-progress and is never partially-built. statements: one per verdict statement, in the same order, each {text, state: as-planned | amended | deviated, ref (optional: the as-built record's section)}, written at the row's outcome; the outcome is derived from them (deviated if any deviated, else amended if any amended, else as planned) and never contradicts asBuilt.state; a unit row, a dropped and a deferred row have none. amended and deviated list changes[]; a change that settles a deferred option carries settles: {option, verdict}. dropped states its reason in summary; deferred names issue. complete (implemented and qa passed, not merged yet; set by the qa-pass event) and landed (merged; set by the pre-merge refresh) are for a tracking board's unit rows only: a unit goes pending, complete, landed. An issue board's rows keep as-planned, amended, deviated.

statements.text: <what was built for the first verdict statement, past tense>
<what was built for the second, and how it differs>

rows.name: <a scope item the plan deliberately leaves alone>

options.name: <leave it, to the issue that owns it>

unit.board: <set by embed.js: NN-slug/dashboard.html once that board exists in this tree, else null (plan/RULES.md §1)>

gap.summary: <what the unit's system lacks at the baseline>

statements.text: <the unit's scope from the decomposition, one decision each>

verdict.defense: <why the unit is scoped as it is: one system, a bug fix, docs only; never its work level>
tests: <the test levels the unit's plan must cover>

impact.$comment: The Consequences tab (plan/RULES.md §2, Consequences; the Impact tab before dashboards-skill/35, its data key impact kept). new.js sets impact to null; the plan-accepted event writes it from consequences.md (impact.md in a folder older than the rename) (and plan.md where it states API or migration facts) with basis plan; its changes[] accumulate as the work lands while basis stays plan (an implementation stage's deviation; on a tracking board, each unit's landing); the landed event (a tracking board's at its last unit's) reconciles it from final-implementation.md and the reconciled consequences.md with basis as-built, keeping each difference from the planned impact in changes[]. basis stores plan or as-built and nothing else: the reconciliation state (planned, partial, as-built) is derived from the data (plan/scripts/lib.js reconciliation(); the template's reconciliationOf()), never stored. none: a plain statement that no downstream impact is recorded, and why, when that is the case (common at level 2; a level-3 change with release.bump none says so). release.bump: none | fix | feat | major; release.unreleased: true (optional) marks a change whose downstream effect lands on a new artifact that has never been released: no existing version moves (bump none) and its first release is its own; record that artifact as a downstream entry of kind artifact. downstream[].kind: consumer | system | repository | artifact | operator; effect: none | additive | behaviour | breaking. adaptation[].need: none | optional | required. api[].change: added | changed | deprecated | removed; tier: stable-core | supported-extension | experimental | internal | null (not stated). conversion[] is ordered. system: a registry slug in systems, or null for a party outside the repository's systems. compat (every entry, optional): compatible | notable | breaking, raising never lowering what the entry's effect, change or need makes it; the Impact tab draws breaking red, notable yellow, compatible in the system's colour (GUIDANCE.md §1). units[] (tracking boards only): one entry per unit row id, summarising that unit's own impact; the board links the unit's board; its changes[] are the unit's own differences from its planned impact, written when its entry is reconciled. changes[]: each difference from the planned impact, recorded as the work lands, never on the Impact tab: the As built tab shows them, beside the rows' changes. unit (tracking boards only): the unit row id whose landing recorded the entry; every landed unit records its effect on the initiative's impact, either the changes it made (each with unit) or one "no change" entry {unit, when, none: true}, which names no entry; check.js warns on a landed unit with neither. entry (optional): the entry it changed, as <section>.<index>, which the As built card links on the Impact tab; system (optional): the registry slug it concerns, else its entry's, else none (muted). Summaries and links only: no listings.
impact.summary: <two to four lines: what the change means outside itself>

units.summary: <the unit's own impact in a sentence or two>

changes.unit: <unit row id: tracking boards only; leave out on an issue board>

tests.$comment: The Tests tab (plan/RULES.md §2, "The Tests tab"); absent or null until a class is recorded, and never on a tracking board (embed.js mirrors each unit's into its row as unit.tests). base: the ref the branch's diff is taken against; updated: the last change. added: the test classes new on the branch; amended: the existing classes the branch changed (both from the diff, growing with each implementation stage); relevant: unchanged existing classes that exercise the new code anyway (what the qa pass's test inspection ran, less added and amended; with each qa pass). A class is in one list only, added before amended before relevant. Each class: class (its name, fully qualified where it has a package), module, testLevel (1 | 2 | 3 | 4a | 4b | 4c | 5, the five-level testing hierarchy's: a test level, never a work level; absent when its package or path names its level folder, testing.<segment>), path, tests (its test count), rows (the ids of the board rows it verifies), stage (the implementation stage that last added or changed it), result {state: passed | failed | skipped | not-run, passed, failed, skipped, pass (the qa pass), at}. other: {byModule: {<module>: {<test level, or none>: <classes> | {classes, tests}}}}, counts only: never run for this change. apply-event.js writes it from an event's facts.tests (testslib.js mergeTests()); otherwise the presenter fills it from the diff and the qa report.
tests.base: <the ref of the diff, e.g. master>

followUps.title: <the issue's title, optional: with it the number opens the GitHub issue and the title its board>

notes.paths: <how paths are abbreviated on this board>
